# Session Environment Demo

This runbook shows how blocks share one session environment. A script sets a variable
for the blocks after it by writing `NAME=value` to the file named by `$RUNBOOK_ENV`.
Anything it only `export`s, and any directory it `cd`s into, stays inside that script.

## Overview

In this demo, we'll:
1. Set environment variables in Block 1
2. Read and set variables from Python
3. Read the variables in a later block
4. Change the variables and verify the new values
5. Set variables with multiline values
6. Run a block in another directory with `workingDir`

---

## 1. Set Initial Environment Variables

Let's start by writing some variables to `$RUNBOOK_ENV`. They're set for all subsequent blocks. The script also exports a variable, which later blocks won't see.

<Command 
    id="set-initial-env"
    path="scripts/set-initial-env.sh"
    title="Set initial environment variables"
    description="This command writes DEMO_VAR, DEMO_COUNT, and DEMO_PROJECT to $RUNBOOK_ENV. These will be available in all subsequent blocks."
    successMessage="Environment variables set successfully!"
    failMessage="Failed to set environment variables."
/>

---

## 1.1 Python Can Read Session Variables

Non-bash scripts like Python can **read** variables set by earlier blocks. This Python script verifies it can access DEMO_VAR, DEMO_COUNT, and DEMO_PROJECT set in Block 1.

<Command 
    id="python-test"
    path="scripts/python-test.py"
    title="Python reads bash env vars"
    description="This Python script reads and verifies the environment variables set by bash in Block 1."
    successMessage="Python successfully read all the session variables!"
    failMessage="Python could not read the environment variables. Run Block 1 first!"
/>

---

## 1.2 Python Can Set Session Variables

`$RUNBOOK_ENV` is a file, so a Python script can append to it too. A change to `os.environ` only affects the Python process.

<Command 
    id="python-set-env"
    path="scripts/python-set-env.py"
    title="Set env vars from Python"
    description="This Python script writes PYTHON_SET_VAR, PYTHON_COUNT, and PYTHON_PROJECT to $RUNBOOK_ENV."
    successMessage="Python script executed!"
    failMessage="Python script failed."
/>

---

## 1.3 Verify the Python Script's Variables

Let's check that the variables the Python script wrote reached this block.

<Check 
    id="verify-python-env"
    path="checks/verify-python-env.sh"
    title="Check Python env vars"
    description="This check verifies whether PYTHON_SET_VAR, PYTHON_COUNT, and PYTHON_PROJECT are available."
    successMessage="The Python script's variables are set!"
    failMessage="The Python script's variables are missing. Run Block 1.2 first."
/>

---

## 1.4 Run an Inline Command with Python

An inline `command` has no file extension, so it runs with bash unless it has a shebang. The `interpreter` prop names another program for it, without a shebang inside the string.

<Command
    id="python-inline"
    interpreter="python3"
    command={`import os, sys
project = os.environ.get("DEMO_PROJECT")
if not project:
    sys.exit("DEMO_PROJECT is not set. Run Block 1 first!")
print(f"Inline Python sees DEMO_PROJECT={project}")`}
    title="Run inline Python"
    description="This inline command runs with python3, which the block names in its interpreter prop."
    successMessage="python3 ran the inline command!"
    failMessage="The inline Python command failed. Run Block 1 first."
/>

---

## 5. Multiline Environment Variables

Variables can contain newlines (RSA keys, JSON configs, multiline strings). Write each one as
`NAME<<DELIMITER`, then the value's lines, then the delimiter on a line of its own.

<Command 
    id="set-multiline-env"
    path="scripts/set-multiline-env.sh"
    title="Set multiline environment variables"
    description="Sets MULTILINE_KEY (simulated RSA key), JSON_CONFIG, and MULTILINE_SIMPLE with embedded newlines."
    successMessage="Multiline environment variables set!"
    failMessage="Failed to set multiline environment variables."
/>

---

## 5.1 Verify Multiline Values

Let's verify that the multiline values were preserved correctly - not truncated at the first newline.

<Check 
    id="verify-multiline-env"
    path="checks/verify-multiline-env.sh"
    title="Verify multiline env vars"
    description="Verifies that MULTILINE_KEY, JSON_CONFIG, and MULTILINE_SIMPLE retained their embedded newlines."
    successMessage="Multiline environment variables preserved correctly!"
    failMessage="Multiline values were corrupted - newlines may have been lost."
/>

---

## 6. Create a Working Directory

This block creates `demo-workdir` in the session's directory and `cd`s into it. The `cd` stays inside the script.

<Command
    id="create-workdir"
    path="scripts/create-workdir.sh"
    title="Create a working directory"
    description="Creates demo-workdir in the session's directory and cd's into it."
    successMessage="Created demo-workdir!"
    failMessage="Failed to create demo-workdir."
/>

---

## 7. A cd Stays in Its Script

This block has no `workingDir`, so it starts in the session's directory, not in `demo-workdir`.

<Check
    id="verify-cd-stays-in-script"
    path="checks/verify-cd-stays-in-script.sh"
    title="Verify the cd stayed in its script"
    description="Checks that this block starts in the session's directory."
    successMessage="This block starts in the session's directory!"
    failMessage="This block didn't start in the session's directory."
/>

---

## 8. Run a Block in Another Directory

Set `workingDir` to run a block somewhere else. A relative path is relative to the session's directory.

<Check
    id="verify-workdir"
    path="checks/verify-workdir.sh"
    workingDir="demo-workdir"
    title="Verify working directory"
    description="This check runs with workingDir=demo-workdir."
    successMessage="This block runs in demo-workdir!"
    failMessage="This block didn't run in demo-workdir. Run Block 6 first."
/>

---

## Summary

If all checks passed, you've seen how blocks share the session:

- **Variables** a script writes to `$RUNBOOK_ENV` are set for subsequent blocks, from any language
- **Writing a variable again** gives later blocks its new value
- **Multiline values** (RSA keys, JSON, etc.) keep their newlines
- **`export` and `cd`** stay inside the script that runs them
- **`workingDir`** picks the directory a block runs in
